newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BAE SEEKS 'PARTNERSHIP' WITH AUSTRALIAN GOVT.
newsitem.headline: BAE SEEKS 'PARTNERSHIP' WITH AUSTRALIAN GOVT.

text.p: British Aerospace Australia Ltd said on Thursday it was seeking to establish a special 'partnership' with the Australian government which would allow it to build a defence industry rather than be focused on limited projects.

"What we want to do is to go from having 57 different projects to having a smaller number of larger projects where we can actually develop a viable industry," BAe Australia group managing director Robin Southwell told Reuters.
The company is owned by British Aerospace Plc.
Southwell said the company wanted a relationship with the government, its main customer, which allowed in-depth discussions on the government's plans and processes.
"We are asking for a partnership relationship with the government, but acknowledging that the government is not exclusively tied to us, that it can look elsewhere," he said.

Southwell said he did not believe it was in the interests of the government that any company which "wants to buy their way into the marketplace" should necessarily have precedence over another which was creating grassroots skills and capabilities.

He said around the world governments were comfortable in creating a close relationship with the defence industry. "We are not saying we should be the sole supplier, what we are saying is we have got something which we hope government will recognise and will allow us to have a closer partnership relationship with the government," he said.
"In the past your ability to develop a relationship with the government is conditioned by only one thing, whether or not you have or have not won a tender, so it is project related."
Southwell was speaking after the opening of BAe Australia's A$5 million refurbishment of its manufacturing facility here.
With BAe Australia's objective to grow revenue to A$1 billion revenue a year, Southwell said it was "moving up to A$300 million plus" from A$100 million just two years ago.
He said BAe was on the lookout for suitable acquisitions and currently looking at the government-owned arms maker and property developer Australian Defence Industries (ADI).

"It is shortly going to come to the market either as a trade sale or as a public float and to that extent we may well be looking at whether or not we can play a part in that," he said, adding his preferred option was to pursue a stake in a float.
BAe Australia was also considering bids for a number of large projects and hoped to win a repeat order for its A$15 million Kuwait military vehicle contract in the next six months.
